name: Panzer IV
about: Made by tools/battle-models (tank). Metres; x forward, y right, z up. A battle model: `part` says which part each point belongs to; `parts` are the parts (parent, pivot, axis of turning, way of sliding); `sockets` are named places for flash, smoke, fire and wake; `clips` move the parts. Turns: +t degrees about an axis carries p to p cos t + (axis x p) sin t + axis (axis . p)(1 - cos t), about the part's pivot. Paints: 0 upper, 1 upper2, 2 shade, 3 track, 4 rubber, 5 steel, 6 bright, 7 wood, 8 canvas, 9 glass, 10 black, 11 rust, 12 lamp, 13 white, 14 red, 15 yellow, 16 blue, 17 leather, 18 torn, 19 rope, 20 cloth, 21 skin, 22 brass, 23 bakelite, 24 upper3 `mid`: the middle mesh, for about 40 to 140 m (~15,000 triangles): the near mesh thinned, small pieces gone, the far mesh's track band in place of the links, alike parts (road wheels) carrying the same mesh; its `part` numbers count the parts without the track links, as `far`'s do.

tracks.left.about: the left track runs on by one link (120 mm): loop it at (that side's speed in m/s) / stride * long; backward to go astern

tracks.right.about: the right track runs on by one link (120 mm): loop it at (that side's speed in m/s) / stride * long; backward to go astern

start.about: the engine is started: she shudders, a gout of smoke from the exhaust

drive.about: under way: the hull's own motion (the game rolls the wheels, runs the tracks and moves her)

move_off.about: she moves off: the nose lifts as the tracks bite, and settles

stop.about: she brakes: start it as the brakes go on. The nose dips and stays down while she slows; she is at rest `rest` seconds in (play it faster or slower to fit), and the nose comes back up, a little over, and settles

fire.about: the main gun fires: flash and blast at 0.0, the barrel runs back at once and out again over a second, the empty case a moment after

fire.rock.about: the hull's answer to the shot, for a gun trained ahead: she is thrown back on her springs, the nose lifts about a degree, and she settles in a second. With the turret trained off, turn this about the turret's bearing or play it weaker

mg_burst.about: a burst from the machine gun beside the main gun: ten rounds

hull_mg_burst.about: a burst from the hull machine gun

roof_mg_burst.about: a burst from the roof machine gun: only while her commander is up in his hatch (open_up) with his hands on grip.roof_mg.l and grip.roof_mg.r, and never with the roof_mg swap off (no gun on her roof). The MG 34 at about 850 rounds a minute

open_up.about: the commander's hatch is opened (she travels opened up; play it backward to close down for action)

knocked_out.about: knocked out: struck at 0.0, hatches thrown open as the crew bail out, the gun droops, smoke, then fire at the engine; holds its last pose (follow with `burn`)

burn.about: burning: fire at the engine and out of her hatches, black smoke (loop after knocked_out or brew_up)

brew_up.about: her ammunition goes: flame jets from the hatches, then the blast throws the turret off its ring to lie beside her; holds its last pose (follow with `burn`)

suspension.how: each road wheel hangs on a swing arm of its own: turn the arm by (how far the ground under that wheel stands above the level she rests on) / metres_per_degree, inside its limits, and the wheel rides up with it; the two arms of a pair bear on one leaf spring, so a pair may also be rocked (one arm up, its partner down by as much). Leave them at 0 on level ground.

camouflage.how: `blend` (point by point, 0 to 100) is how far a point of the coat is into the second coat colour: camouflage blotches. Fill `upper` with the nation's paint and `upper2` with its paint2; a nation with one colour only: fill `upper2` with `upper`. `blend2` (the same, where the mesh has it) is how far the point is into a third coat colour, `upper3`, sprayed over the second where they meet: colour = mix(mix(upper, upper2, blend), upper3, blend2). A reader that knows only `blend` shows two colours.

dust_is: road dirt: `dust` (0 to 100 a point) is how far the point's finished paint has gone to `dust_colour`; thick low on her, thin by her shoulders, on her tracks too. (`wear` is still paint chipped to the metal, as it was.) A mark's own `dust` dulls it the same way: paint the mark, then take it that far to `dust_colour`. Work it out on the coat she wears (after a paint swap; a swap's choice may name its own dust_colour and haze_colour), from these numbers: the .glb's COLOR_0 is the same thing worked out for the coat she was built in. A game on other ground may use that ground's own colour. Lay no other dust, sun fade or camouflage of the game's own over a file that has `dust`. `haze` (0 to 100, where the mesh has it) is the thin pale dust lying on what looks up: after `dust`, take the point that far to `haze_colour`.
shade_is: `shade` (0 to 1 a point, where the mesh has it, as the soldiers' files have it) is how open the point is to the sky: multiply the point's finished colour by it. The shadow in her creases, which the battle's light does not cast.

turret.what: trained by the game: + to the right (clockwise from above)

gun.what: laid by the game inside its limits: + muzzle up

roof_mg.what: aimed by the game inside the two parts' limits, and only while her commander is up (open_up played) with his hands on grip.roof_mg.l and grip.roof_mg.r: roof_mg + to the right, roof_mg_cradle + muzzle up. With no commander up it is not fired, and with the file's roof_mg swap on `off` she has no roof gun at all: never aim it or play roof_mg_burst. The mount rides the rail round his cupola, so roof_mg turns about the cupola's middle: turn him with it (his facing is roof_mg's bearing). Draw the gun itself (roof_mg_cradle) only while he mans it, and scale it to nothing otherwise (crews kept the MG 34 inside till they needed it; parked anywhere, its stock would hang over the open hatch where he stands): the carriage, roof_mg, stays.

swaps.how: one model for the whole war. gun: show the chosen gun's parts and scale the other's to nothing (a part scaled to nothing is not drawn), and use its sockets in place of the default ones. paint: put the chosen coat's colours in place of the paints of the same names. by_month: the face she wore in each month of a campaign, one row per run of months (from and to are both counted in), naming the choice of each swap. Where a row gives a `mix`, both served side by side: each vehicle of a unit draws its own choice by those shares, and a game that shows one face a unit takes `one`. zimmerit: the ribbed paste on her upright plates, as real ribs (no texture is needed): show the choice's parts, or scale them to nothing for a tank without it. Near mesh only: the far mesh has none. roof_mg: the machine gun on her roof that only her commander fires. `on`: show the choice's parts; `off`: scale them to nothing, and then the game must not aim or fire a roof gun at all (no roof_mg_burst; controls.roof_mg left alone).

camo.what: dark yellow with olive green and red-brown sprayed over it in the field

desert42.what: light brown, the desert coat of 1942

by_ground.how: by_ground: on a field of this ground (the field's look: desert) the rows here are read before by_month, as by_month is read (from and to both counted in; a row with neither holds every month), and pick the coat; a month no row holds falls back to by_month. `under` is the colour that shows where the coat is worn through (the pictures' chips; the game's own wear may use it).

off.years: to August 1943, and on tanks built after September 1944

on.what: ribbed paste on her upright plates

off.what: no gun on her roof: the game must then not aim or fire a roof gun (no roof_mg_burst)
off.years: 1939 to April 1943: no rail on her cupola (and a tank of any year whose crew kept the gun inside)

on.what: an MG 34 on the anti-aircraft rail round her cupola

long.what: 7.5 cm L/43 and L/48, double-baffle muzzle brake

on.what: thin plates hung on rails along her hull, a shield round her turret's sides and back
on.years: 1943-05 on, with the dark yellow coat

lose.how: each tank hides none, one or two of these hull plates at random, so a company is not one tank copied; the rails and the turret's shield always stay

name_place.how: Once her unit has come through three battles the game paints her crew's mark here. kind `name`: an invented name (four to ten letters to a line) in brush-painted capitals, never a printed face: the middle of it at `at` on the plate that looks along `facing`, the writing running along `along` with its top toward `up`, the letters `high` tall and the whole no longer than that place's `long`; it rides `part`, and a place is given for each side that carries one. A name too long for one line at `high`: on two lines where the place has `lines` 2 and the name two words (letters `high_two` tall, or `high` where that is not given), else painted smaller, but never under `least`; a name that fits neither way is not for this tank. `writing` down: the characters stand one under another, `long` the room downward. `script` japanese: her name is in Japanese characters, and only the names in brush-alphabet.json `japanese.names` have theirs drawn; for any other name paint nothing (never Latin letters on her); a name of a single character is `high_one` tall. kind `rings`: no name, but `most` thin bands round the barrel, the first at `at` and each next one `step` on along `toward` (to the breech), `wide` across, lying on the barrel whose radius there is `radius`; one ring, then more as she lasts. `ink`: for a name off-white on grey, olive and green coats and near-black on dark yellow; rings off-white on every coat. Matt, never brighter than her national marking; it wears and scorches with her paint.
name_place.when: her unit has come through three battles

running.how: turn each wheel by (distance run on its side) / radius, in radians; play tracks.left and tracks.right at (speed of that side) / stride * long
